bull_bear.body:
- As on 30th June 2026 (Standalone) the deck states Capital Employed of Rs. 105,910 crore, Net Worth of Rs. 70,658 crore and LT Loan Outstanding of Rs. 13,823 crore.
- Debt Equity Ratio is shown rising across the series: 0.22 (FY23), 0.29 (FY24), 0.26 (FY25), 0.28 (FY26) and 0.32 (Q1 FY27).
- Equity of Rs. 77,593 crore comprises Equity Share Capital of Rs. 6,575 crore and Other Equity of Rs. 71,018 crore, within which Retained Earnings are Rs. 63,956 crore.
- A footnote records that "Share Price & EPS for past periods are adjusted for Bonus issue & Buy Back", indicating both have occurred, though the deck gives no dates or amounts.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- The deck identifies GAIL (India) Limited as "A Government of India Undertaking - A Maharatna Company", presenting under the tagline "Energizing Possibilities".
- The deck frames the business around four physical performance lines - Natural Gas Transmission, Natural Gas Marketing, LPG Transmission, and Petrochemical / Liquid Hydrocarbons sales - reported on a standalone basis, alongside a separate consolidated set.

business.body:
- [Disclosure basis] The deck is the Investors' & Analysts' Presentation for Q1 FY 2026-27, filed under Regulation 30 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and dated 31.07.2026.
- [Standalone vs consolidated] The deck reports both standalone and consolidated sets; the balance sheet, physical performance and key ratios are standalone only, so group-level asset and leverage detail is not disclosed.

deepdive.thesis: GAIL (India) Ltd is India's state-owned leader in natural gas transmission and marketing, driving the nation's energy transition through expanded infrastructure, petrochemicals, and pioneering green hydrogen and biogas initiatives.

open.item: GAIL is setting up a 500 KTA Propane Dehydrogenation and Polypropylene (PDH-PP) plant at Usar, Maharashtra - India's first PDH-technology Propylene plant - with all equipment delivered and construction in progress; commissioning targeted for FY 2027-28.
Company plans to expand the Dabhol LNG terminal's regasification capacity from 5.0 MMTPA to 6.3 MMTPA in the first phase over the next 3 years, enabling it to handle up to 100 LNG cargoes annually.
Company looks to expand the Dabhol LNG terminal's regasification capacity from 5.0 MMTPA to 6.3 MMTPA in the first phase over the next 3 years.
The CBG Blending Obligation (CBO) envisages phased blending of Compressed Biogas in CGD networks up to 5% by FY 2028-29, for which GAIL was designated the nodal agency for gas pooling.
GAIL will produce Polypropylene (PP) products, branded 'G-Pro', at its upcoming PP Plant at Usar.

GAIL's strategic initiative to revive the PTA plant at wholly-owned subsidiary GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited (GMPL) is nearing completion, with commercial production expected to commence very soon.

Company is executing two captive liquid pipelines - the 357 km Vijaipur-Pata C2/C3 pipeline and the 44 km Uran-Usar Propane Pipeline - to feed the Pata Petrochemical Complex and the upcoming PDH-PP plant at Usar; work is in an advanced stage nearing completion.

GAIL is building a new 30-acre R&D Centre at IMT Sohna, Haryana, with world-class laboratory infrastructure, advanced analytical facilities and pilot-scale demonstration units; land possession was taken on 22 February 2026.
Company was accorded approval for laying a 115 km spur line from the Dabhol-Bangalore Pipeline to JSW Vijayanagar, Ballari, for `537.37 crore.
Company approved investment for laying a ~105 km spur line from Vijaipur to BPCL Bina Refinery under the HVJ-GREP-DVPL pipeline.

GAIL is forward-integrating into fertilisers with two proposed plants along the MNJPL corridor - at Saoner (Maharashtra) and Rajnandgaon (Chhattisgarh) - each with capacity of 1.27 MMTPA urea and 0.73 MMTPA ammonia, for an estimated total investment of `21,000 crore; MoUs signed with the Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra governments and a consultant appointed for DFR preparation.

open.item: GAIL committed to invest `3,800 crore in 700 MW of Solar Power Projects in Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.
Company submitted bids for three new PNGRB-tendered LPG pipelines: Cherlapally-Nagpur (~550 km), Jhansi-Sitarganj (~605 km) and Shikrapur to Goa & Hubli (~620 km).
GAIL Mangalore Petrochemicals Limited's PTA plant is expected to be commissioned soon; sub-system and systems commissioning activities are in progress in a phase-wise manner.
Balance works of MNJPL, SAPL and KKBMPL-II pipelines are being expedited and management remains hopeful of completing these projects within the current calendar year.
Company approved capacity augmentation of the DUPL-DPPL pipeline (30" x 105 km) from 19.9 MMSCMD to 22.5 MMSCMD for `844 crore.

drhp.business: GAIL (India) Limited is a Government of India Maharatna company operating India's largest integrated natural gas value chain, spanning natural gas and LPG pipeline transmission, natural gas marketing and LNG trading, petrochemicals (Polyethylene/Polypropylene), LPG and other liquid hydrocarbon (LHC) production, exploration & production, and City Gas Distribution through subsidiaries and joint ventures. It serves Fertilizer, Power, City Gas Distribution and industrial customers (Refinery, Steel, Sponge Iron, Petrochemical) across India, with a small overseas natural gas trading presence.

drhp.expansion: GAIL's FY2025-26 expansion centred on natural gas pipeline build-out: ~2,000 km of pipeline was commissioned during the year, including large sections of the Mumbai-Nagpur-Jharsuguda Pipeline (MNJPL, ~1,504 of 1,707 km), the Srikakulam-Angul Pipeline (SAPL, ~470 of 744 km) and progress on the Kochi-Koottanad-Bengaluru-Mangaluru Phase II (KKBMPL-II) project in Tamil Nadu. A further ~1,500 km of gas pipeline projects remain under execution across multiple states (Kolkata-Haldia, Dhamra-Haldia, Nagpur-Jharsuguda, SAPL spurlines, KKBMPL-II, Gurdaspur-Jammu, DUPL-DPPL augmentation and various spur …

risks.note: Management flags delay in execution of pipeline and process-plant projects as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; large ongoing projects (MNJPL, SAPL, KKBMPL-II, PDH-PP Usar, GMPL PTA) carry commissioning-timeline risk.
risks.risk: Project execution delay risk - pipeline and process plant projects

risks.note: Listed as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; the Company's own five-year data shows Natural Gas Transmission installed capacity utilisation moving in a range, reflecting demand/off-take variability against a large fixed pipeline network.
risks.risk: Underutilization of the Natural Gas pipeline asset base

risks.note: Explicitly flagged as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk; potential regulatory-driven unbundling or monetisation of GAIL's pipeline network could alter its integrated business model and asset ownership.
risks.risk: Restructuring risk - monetization/unbundling of pipeline assets

risks.note: Adverse movement of crude oil/LNG prices, shortage of LNG cargoes, an expected increase in domestic gas volumes, and risk of LNG contract default by upstream suppliers are flagged; GAIL largely imports LNG, capital goods and stores & spares, adding foreign-exchange exposure that is managed under its Foreign Currency & Interest Rate Risk Management Policy and Commodity Price Risk Management (CPRM) Policy.

Risk of reduced Petrochemical margins from higher imports, lower prices and high input costs; specific risk of unviable operations at the Pata plant due to higher feedstock cost, and at the Pata/Vijaipur C2-C3 plant due to reduced availability of C2-C3 in feed gas.

Flagged risks include reduction of APM (Administered Price Mechanism) gas allocation, decrease in market share of domestic gas, inability to acquire new volumes of domestic gas, and shutdown of ONGC facilities that supply feed gas.

Explosion or high-fatality leakage risk is flagged across LPG & NG pipelines and their RT/SV stations, Petrochemical and GPU/C2-C3 recovery plants, and CGD NG pipelines, alongside risk of third-party damage and encroachment and broader natural/man-made calamity risk (blowout, earthquake, tsunami, terrorism); mitigated via design standards, an Emergency Response and Disaster Management Plan, and a Mega Insurance/Large Risk Insurance policy.
risks.risk: Pipeline/plant safety and third-party damage risk

risks.note: Management flags inadequate controls to protect systems against malicious attacks as a Top Corporate Level Key Risk, which could result in loss of data and disruption of operations.
